messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident INC-9876 opened by monitoring — sudden p99 streaming tail latency spike across eu-west2 -> eu-central cross-zone paths. Affected: streaming RPCs and some text-gen workloads.
Alex: Paging oncall — looks like p95 up ~3x, p99 > 10s on streaming tails, customer-facing errors reported.
Maria: Got the page, joining. Any obvious config deploys?
Jon: No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.
Danielle: I'm seeing a sudden uptick in TLS handshake retries in the egress NAT metrics for eu-west2 to eu-central.
Ryan: Logs show a lot of TCP retransmits and DNS lookup timeouts for our crosszone edge LB.
Eva: Reproduced a streaming stall locally by forcing a cross-zone route — stalls on recv for ~8-12s, then recovers.
Alex: Ok, triage plan: 1) confirm scope and customer impact 2) check NAT ephemeral exhaustion 3) validate DNS and TLS handshake rates 4) attempt mitigation (reroute / failover).
Maria: Customer impact: two customers in EU reported degraded streaming sessions and 503s. Alerts: error-rate-route-X high.
Jon: Metric snippets: 
``` 
metric:streaming_tail_p99{region="eu-west2"} = 10.8s
metric:streaming_tail_p95{region="eu-west2"} = 1.9s
metric:tls_handshake_errors{path="crosszone"} increased x6 in 5m
metric:udp_dns_timeout_rate{zone_pair="euw-euc"} = 4.2% (baseline 0.1%)
```
Danielle: NAT stats: ephemeral port usage at 89% on nat-gw-12, conntrack spikes visible. Potential port exhaustion or excessive retransmit leading to handshake failures.
Ryan: Traceroute from edge -> nat shows hairpin via transit router with high latency ~120ms vs expected 20ms.
Eva: Also seeing delayed SYN-ACKs in packet captures, followed by client retransmits.
Alex: Can someone run the cross-zone path healthcheck script and paste output? runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/xcrosszone
Danielle: Running now, output: 
```
> ./xcrosszone-check --pair euw-euc --samples 50
50/50 dns_ok
50/50 syn_sent
45/50 syn_ack_delayed
rtt median 110ms
packet_loss 2.3%
```
Maria: That's consistent with packet loss + queuing in transit. Could be a routing flap or NAT gateway overloaded.
Jon: Check cloud provider NAT scaling — I see a scale activity spike at 2501234000 but then it flattened. Possible scaling jitter.
Alex: Mitigation options: A) fail traffic to alternate NAT pool in same AZ, B) force local egress (avoid cross-zone), C) roll traffic to eu-central-only nodes, D) temporarily increase TLS handshake timeouts on client side — risky.
Eva: Quick test: can we add a policy to force streaming traffic to prefer local egress (disable cross-zone) for eu-west2? That would reduce crosszone TLS flows.
Danielle: I can flip a routing preference on the border router to prefer local egress for the streaming route. It'll apply in ~30s.
Ryan: Before flipping, any impact to reserved/dedicated workloads? Check Dedicated customers pinned to specific egress.
Maria: Verified dedicated customers unaffected — they have pinned routes. Only shared-hosted streaming is on the affected path.
Alex: Do the flip. Post the command you run.
Danielle: Running: 
```
# prefer-local-egress for route streaming-service
rbctl set-policy streaming-service --egress-preference local --scope eu-west2
```
Danielle: policy applied, waiting for convergence.
ops-bot: Routing policy change applied by Danielle at 2501234680, change id rp-54321.
Eva: Seeing immediate drop in crosszone TLS handshake errors on the monitoring panel. p99 dropping from 10.8s -> 3.2s within 60s.
Jon: Packet loss on crosszone path dropping too. nat-gw-12 ephemeral usage still high though.
Alex: Good. Next: verify long-lived sessions recovery and start a controlled canary for the affected customers.
Maria: Can we also trigger a NAT pool failover to a fresh pool to free ephemeral ports? Danielle can coordinate with cloud infra.
Danielle: Kicking a NAT pool failover to nat-gw-24, should be seamless. command: 
```
cloudctl nat failover --from nat-gw-12 --to nat-gw-24 --async
```
Danielle: Failover initiated.
Ryan: Logs show client retries decreasing, tcp retransmits down 70%.
Eva: Streaming consumer metrics returning to baseline, p95 ~0.6s, p99 ~1.1s for EU after both mitigations.
Alex: Great. Assemble blameless summary items: suspected cause = NAT scaling jitter + transient cross-zone routing queueing causing TLS handshake spikes and delayed SYN-ACKs -> streaming stalls. Mitigations = prefer-local-egress + NAT failover.
Maria: Action items: 1) follow-up with cloud provider on NAT scaling behavior (assigned Danielle) 2) add alert for ephemeral port >80% + conntrack rises (assigned Ryan) 3) update runbook to include prefer-local-egress play (assigned Alex) 4) customer follow-up (assigned Maria).
Danielle: Filing ticket with provider: TICKET-CLD-7744 with packet captures and scaling timeline.
Jon: I'm going to run a postmortem check in 1h to ensure no recurrence.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Closing the paging loop. Incident remains in monitoring for 30m.
incident-bot: INC-9876 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Notifying oncall rotation for handoff.
Maria: I'll draft status for customers and ops.
Eva: Leaving a note in the streaming dashboard about the temporary egress preference change and revert plan.
Alex: Revert plan: if metrics stable for 60m, revert policy and route back with controlled canary to ensure cloud NAT didn't fully recover.
ops-bot: Handoff to next oncall at 2501234899: Maria will be primary for follow-ups.
Maria: Acknowledged.
Alex: End of thread.
